name: brounger

attributes.attribute: British spirit that haunts the east coast
levies a tax of fish upon fisherfolk
may have descended from a Celtic thunder god

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The brounger is a spirit of British legend. It haunts the east coast. It levies a tax of fish upon fisherfolk. The being may have descended from a Celtic thunder god. It stands among the spirits of British tradition.

okr.objective: Describe the brounger as a coastal spirit that taxes fishermen.
key_results: The brounger haunts the eastern coast of Britain.
It levies a tax of fish upon fisherfolk.
The spirit may descend from a Celtic thunder god.
